analysis.title: GS Pasquariello - markets / macro 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 keeps rising and NDX made a higher high despite pressure across global bond markets. Equal-weight S&P is down seven straight weeks, which can be read as poor breadth or as the difficulty of beating cap-weighted S&P led by US mega cap tech.
Q3 performance split: Magnificent Seven +11%, cap-weighted S&P +2%, equal-weight S&P -2%, Russell -8%. US 10-year yields rose 82 bps over the quarter.

Leaders are leading on earnings growth and laggards are lagging on rates and oil. Momentum factor was -30% in July, -14% in August and +27% in September, so fast-money trading is harder than it looks.

US tech has reasserted market leadership: META is up 25% over the past month on agentic AI optimism, MU rallied on strong earnings despite a large market cap and a high multiple, and NVDA added $150bn to its buyback, bringing the total to $235bn, with nearly $300bn of market cap added since the announcement.

NDX has rallied in 11 of the past 13 days despite higher interest rates. The desk attributes this to fundamental news flow at the mega caps, which is the one part of the market with clear capital inflows.
A GS Asia equities colleague notes some global investors remain underweight a region where some of the largest companies have sell-side price targets implying about 90% upside.
Japan has outperformed the S&P YTD: TOPIX +20.0% in local terms vs roughly +11.8% for the S&P, and the Nikkei +36.6%.

On Iran, there is a lot of talk and no progress, and the desk expects tension to rise. Persian Gulf oil exports are back to the 2025 average, so the oil market has adapted. The war remains an open risk for stocks.

Desk likes the technical setup for the S&P despite many worries, with the index stuck near 7700. Quarter-end and month-end supply is behind the market, long-only and levered funds have cut length, buybacks should accelerate as Q3 reporting proceeds, and US retail was inactive in September.
Foreign investors are still pouring into US equities despite repeated calls for de-dollarization.
The desk is skeptical European equities can compete with US and Asian equities in the next round given mounting pressure on EU sovereign debt.
Key Q4 question is whether US mega cap tech can stay 'duration resistant' as global 10-year yields rise.

market_movers.rationale: META is up 25% over the past month on the presumed birth of agentic AI for the US consumer.
MU rallied on superb earnings despite a huge market cap and a stubborn multiple.
NVDA added $150bn to its buyback plan, now $235bn in total, with nearly $300bn of market cap expansion since the announcement.

sector_views.rationale: Leadership reasserted on strong earnings growth and buybacks, with the group still making higher highs despite higher rates.
Gathering pressure across EU sovereign debt makes it hard for them to compete with US and Asian equities.

earnings_insights: MU rallied on superb earnings despite a large market cap and a high multiple. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.
Q3 earnings reporting is starting and buybacks should kick fully into gear as it proceeds.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Sharp rise in US rates is pressuring laggards and breadth, while mega cap tech has held up.

risk_factors: Gathering pressure across global bond markets and higher US yields.
Iran war and oil supply risk.
Poor market breadth, with equal-weight S&P down seven straight weeks.
vol_and_positioning: Long-only funds and the levered community have clearly shed length.
Momentum factor returns were -30% in July, -14% in August and +27% in September.
Quarter-end and month-end supply is behind the market, and US retail investors were inactive in September.
Buybacks are expected to accelerate as the Q3 reporting period moves along.
geopolitical: Iran: lots of talk, no progress, and the desk expects the temperature to rise.
Persian Gulf oil exports are back to the average level of 2025, so the oil market has adapted to the conflict.

tension_points.theme: US mega cap tech vs rates
tension_points.bull_case: Mega caps keep making higher highs on superb earnings growth and large buybacks, and NDX rose in 11 of the past 13 days despite higher yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Global 10-year yields are rising sharply (US 10s +82 bps in Q3) and equal-weight S&P is down seven straight weeks, so the rally is narrow.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report frames the Q4 question as whether mega cap tech can remain 'duration resistant', but names no specific level.
